solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: As Britain was: Ali suffers

parts.note: the punctuation mark in the clue is itself a colon, read as its name

indicators.note: to suffer is to be knocked about, so the letters of Ali are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark on Britain's past, as if a boxer named Ali were paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon is not mere punctuation: the mark itself supplies COLON. 'suffers' rearranges ALI into IAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain once ruled an empire of overseas possessions, so it was an imperial, colony-holding power.

clue.text: Firm bottom? That's rude!

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone protests that mentioning a backside is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSE is British slang for buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude or vulgar language is described as rough and unrefined.

clue.text: A telly production in recent times

indicators.note: a production is something made up, so these letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A television show made not long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently, in the last little while, means the same as this adverb.

clue.text: Cuts devil's takes: nothing to report

definitions.meaning: Old Nick is the devil, so belonging to him
to nick is British slang for to steal

indicators.note: to report is to say aloud, so the word is heard

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A gangster's knifings and the devil's haul, but nothing to tell the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions plus a sound-alike: NIX, slang for nothing, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small cuts, Old Nick's possessive and British slang for steals all share this spelling.

clue.text: In the morning girl is continent

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
Erica is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl landing on a new continent at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World landmass, North and South together, is a continent.

clue.text: 12.5% extra wonder

definitions.meaning: twelve and a half per cent is one part in eight
the '... wonder of the world' is a marvel added beyond the classical seven

explanation.surface: An added marvel worth a precise percentage.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in eight is 12.5 per cent; a new marvel is dubbed the next after the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: Kind of soldier, embracing left instead of right, turns into guerrilla

indicators.note: turning into something means changing form, so the letters are reordered
here one letter stands in place of another when the two words are compared

explanation.surface: A soldier who goes off-book and becomes a rebel fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards from the answer: put L in place of one R, and 'turns into' rearranges it as GUERRILLA. So swap an L in GUERRILLA for R and rearrange; 'embracing' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular troops are not part of a standing army, like militias or partisans.

clue.text: Important to give this to Richard, but not all of it

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer sits within it

explanation.surface: Something significant to hand over to a man called Richard, but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A momentous event is one that will be remembered by later generations.

clue.text: Perhaps their age is past

definitions.note: the noun sense: what has gone before and been handed down

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible alternative form, so the letters may be reordered

explanation.surface: Speculating that some people's era is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's inherited traditions and history are its legacy from former times.

clue.text: Struck with hotel fork in a relationship

indicators.note: split as 'for K', this says a letter goes in place of the K

parts.note: to strike someone is to attack them
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hit with a piece of hotel cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fork' is not cutlery: read it as 'for K', so H from 'hotel' replaces the K of ATTACKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attached is romantically committed, not single, as a partner is.

clue.text: Rubber queen playing herself?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
an actor playing a role appears as that character
the queen herself is again ER

explanation.surface: A monarch acting in a film as herself.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'queen playing herself' as ER AS ER: the queen, cast 'as', the same queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the stationery item for rubbing out pencil marks.

clue.text: Extremely unappealing (literally)

indicators.note: the extremes of each word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something said to be very off-putting, emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'unappealing' and of 'literally' together spell the answer, which itself means extremely unappealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very unattractive is hideous to look at.

clue.text: Spanish girl heartlessly frolicking and having fun in the pool?

indicators.note: letters romping about playfully are rearranged
with its heart removed, the word girl keeps only its two ends

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl playing in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves GL from 'girl'; 'frolicking' shuffles SPANISH with GL.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing in water means slapping and throwing it about, a typical bit of pool fun.

clue.text: Spirit of Van Gogh, ostensibly

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: Seemingly the soul of the Dutch painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'Gogh' and the start of 'ostensibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit is a spectre, the apparition of a dead person.

clue.text: Not quite up to moment for a place to sit

indicators.note: not quite complete, so the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: 'up to the present moment' is 'so far'

explanation.surface: Seeking a seat, but not quite there yet.
explanation.walkthrough: SO FAR, meaning up to now, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is upholstered seating for several people.

clue.text: How sniper shot into property

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A marksman firing into a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Property is what one possesses, so it stands for possession or title.

clue.text: Lengthy lie over, bar the shouting

indicators.note: a thing knocked over is upset, so these letters are mixed
bar here means except, so those letters are left out of the mix

explanation.surface: A long falsehood finished, apart from the noisy aftermath.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange LENGTHY LIE ('over') after taking out the letters of THE ('bar'); the seven left make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising your voice loudly is synonymous with bawling or hollering.

clue.text: Polishes right away suddenly can't be seen

indicators.note: right is abbreviated to its letter, and away means that letter is sent off out of the word

parts.note: varnishes give wood a polished finish

explanation.surface: A finish that disappears at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means R removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disappears abruptly drops out of sight.

clue.text: Border terrier's clothing: fine or foul?

indicators.note: foul means messed up, so the letters are jumbled
clothing is the outside, so the word's outer letters are used

explanation.surface: A Border terrier's coat in good or bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside of 'terrier' gives TR; 'foul' mixes it with FINEOR. A Border terrier is a British dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary between countries, or the edge of settled land, is a frontier.

clue.text: Head for Rocky Mountains, after a fix

indicators.note: after says this mountain piece follows the letters before it
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: Heading off to the Rockies after a repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head for Rocky' is R; RANGE comes 'after' A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something, such as a meeting, is to organise or set it up.

clue.text: Ambassador has no love for sin

indicators.note: lacking it, the word loses that letter

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent abroad
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A diplomat who is loveless and wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetousness is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Green for stop

definitions.meaning: a green is public parkland, a village grassy space
to stop a vehicle is to leave it standing

explanation.surface: A traffic light colour that, oddly, means halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is open public grass; to pull up and leave a car is to do this.

clue.text: Advance secures origins of best literature into print

indicators.note: securing something holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to push is to press forward

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A step forward in getting fine books printed.
explanation.walkthrough: BL, the initials of 'best literature', goes inside PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book is to bring it out in printed form.

clue.text: Not good as a candle

definitions.meaning: a candle has a wick, so it is furnished with one

explanation.surface: A judgement that something is bad, like a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinful conduct is evil; a candle is literally fitted with a wick.

clue.text: In Copenhagen, cycling means business

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Bicycling in the Danish capital is a serious matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is a firm providing a service, such as travel or advertising.

clue.text: Intimate meal with no starter

indicators.note: lacking its starter, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: dinner is a main meal

explanation.surface: A cosy dinner where nobody orders a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the menu course, but it means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate thoughts are private and deep, the closest ones kept within.

clue.text: Scandinavian king briefly deposed by enfant terrible, buzzing

indicators.note: a ruler deposed by someone is ousted and replaced, so one piece takes another's place

parts.note: a Viking was a Scandinavian seafarer
K is the short form of king, as in chess
an enfant terrible is a badly behaved child, a brat

explanation.surface: A Nordic monarch overthrown by an unruly upstart, amid excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAT replaces the K in VIKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something buzzing hums with rapid tremors, quivering quickly.

clue.text: One's performance right to bag Oscar

indicators.note: bagging something holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an act is a performance
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's turn deserved an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award, but it is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: The defined person is one who performs, a player on stage or screen.

clue.text: Top five playing

indicators.note: playing about, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross-reference to the solution of 5-across

explanation.surface: The five best players at a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'five' is not a number here: it points to 5 across, whose answer is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of something is its peak or highest point, its summit.

clue.text: Wrong girl abducted according to reports

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: a miss is a girl; abducted means taken

explanation.surface: News reports of a kidnapping that turn out false.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS TAKEN, a girl abducted, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in error is to be incorrect, wide of the mark.

clue.text: Scrap band

definitions.meaning: a scrap of material may be a narrow strip of it
a band is a line of colour, as on a flag or a sergeant's sleeve

explanation.surface: A rock group splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth or a coloured band across a surface are both meant here.

clue.text: Had rusty wreck on which child will go far?

definitions.text: on which child will go far?

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An old rusty car that will still take a child a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Monday's child' says the child born on this day 'has far to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the traditional rhyme about birthdays, this weekday's child has far to go.
